🧠 So what does this mean for you?

  • Your fastest path is MERN + TypeScript, not Java. You already have HTML/CSS/JS — extending that into React and Node is the shortest distance between you and an offer.
  • Backend is where freshers win offers. "Knows React" is common; "shipped an authenticated API with error handling" is rare in a fresher pile.
  • Kerala is service-heavy (Infopark/Technopark JDs often say Java + Angular), but Python + React full-stack fresher roles are live too. Keep Java for year 2.
  • Power BI is a differentiator, not a core skill. It makes you interesting for data-adjacent roles — it won't get you a full-stack job on its own.
  • Apply beyond Kerala. 70% Kerala + 30% Bengaluru/Chennai/Hyderabad/remote roughly 5× your market for the same effort.

The training arc

Your 32-week roadmap

Nine seasons. Each one ends with a boss you must actually defeat — a deployed project, not a finished playlist. Tick each topic as you go.

The nindō rule

“I never go back on my word. That's my ninja way.”

You will not feel motivated every day — Naruto didn't either. What carried him was a rule, not a mood. Yours: never skip two days in a row. Miss Monday? Fine. Tuesday is non-negotiable.

01
🎮 ACADEMY ARC · Week 1–2

Setup, Git & HTML/CSS Pro

⏱ 24h 0%

Lock your tools, master Git, and sharpen HTML/CSS until your UI looks hireable. You already know the basics — this arc turns them into proof.

🐲 Boss to defeat: A responsive 3-page portfolio site, deployed live, with 10+ GitHub commits and a real pull request.

Watch / read (verified links)

  • Complete Git and GitHub Tutorial ↗Kunal Kushwaha1h15m · English
  • HTML & CSS Full Course – Beginner to Pro ↗SuperSimpleDev6h30m · English
  • Frontend Roadmap (read, don't binge) ↗roadmap.sh30m · reference

💡 Rule: every day ends with a commit. A green GitHub square is your new high score.

02
⚡ CHAKRA CONTROL ARC · Week 3–7

JavaScript Deep Dive

⏱ 70h 0%

JavaScript is 80% of every full-stack interview. This is the arc where you stop copying code and start understanding it.

🐲 Boss to defeat: 3 vanilla JS apps deployed: Todo (localStorage), Weather (live API), Quiz (timer + score).

Watch / read (verified links)

  • JavaScript Tutorial Full Course – Beginner to Pro (2024) ↗SuperSimpleDev22h · English
  • Namaste JavaScript (Season 1 + 2) ↗Akshay SainiPlaylist · English
  • The Modern JavaScript Tutorial ↗javascript.infoReference · read daily

💡 Watch at 1.5×, then close the video and rebuild the feature from memory. If you can't, you didn't learn it yet.

03
🔥 POWER-UP ARC · Week 8–11

React + TypeScript + Tailwind

⏱ 80h 0%

Stop thinking in pages. Start thinking in components, state and props. TypeScript is now expected in Indian product-company JDs, not optional.

🐲 Boss to defeat: React + TypeScript 'Expense Tracker' with routing, charts, filters and persistence — deployed.

Watch / read (verified links)

  • Chai aur React ↗Hitesh Choudhary (chai aur code)~20h · Hindi/Hinglish
  • TypeScript playlist ↗Hitesh Choudhary~5h · Hindi/Hinglish
  • Learn React (official docs) ↗react.devReference · English
  • Tailwind CSS docs ↗tailwindcss.comReference

💡 Do not start Redux yet. Context + hooks is enough for fresher interviews. Depth beats checkbox collecting.

04
🏰 BACKEND DUNGEON ARC · Week 12–16

Node.js + Express + MongoDB

⏱ 90h 0%

Your first real API. Auth, validation, error handling, deployment — the exact things interviewers probe when they hear 'I know MERN'.

🐲 Boss to defeat: A production-style REST API (Job Board) with JWT auth, roles, pagination, docs and a Postman collection — deployed.

Watch / read (verified links)

  • Complete Backend Developer Course (chai aur backend) ↗Hitesh Choudhary~30h · Hindi/Hinglish
  • Node.js Crash Course Tutorial ↗The Net Ninja4h30m · English
  • MongoDB free courses ↗MongoDB UniversitySelf-paced · English

💡 If your API isn't deployed with a live URL in the README, most recruiters will never see it. Deploy in week 12, not week 16.

Halfway checkpoint · around day 110

“Go beyond. PLUS ULTRA!”

If the authenticated API is deployed, you are no longer “an intern who knows HTML”. You are a full-stack developer with a smaller portfolio. This is the exact point where most people quit — the second half is where the offers live.

05
🗺️ SIDE QUEST ARC · Week 17–18

SQL + Python (Kerala JD insurance)

⏱ 45h 0%

A large share of Kerala JDs ask for SQL or Python. You don't need to become a data scientist — you need to be dangerous enough to survive a technical round.

🐲 Boss to defeat: A 5-table SQL schema + 20 queries for your capstone, plus a small Python CLI and a 2-endpoint Flask/Django API.

Watch / read (verified links)

  • MySQL Tutorial for Beginners [Full Course] ↗Programming with Mosh3h10m · English
  • Python Tutorial – Python for Beginners ↗Programming with Mosh6h · English
  • Django official tutorial (or Flask quickstart) ↗Django docs3h · English

💡 Python tip: don't do a 40-hour data-science course. 15 focused hours + one working script beats 40 hours of videos.

06
🐉 FINAL BOSS ARC · Week 19–22

Capstone + Docker + CI/CD

⏱ 70h 0%

One full-stack product you can demo for 5 minutes without notes. This is the project that carries your resume, your interviews and your confidence.

🐲 Boss to defeat: 'SkillBridge' — a full-stack app (auth, roles, CRUD, dashboard) deployed live with Docker + GitHub Actions.

Watch / read (verified links)

  • Docker Tutorial for Beginners [FULL COURSE in 3 Hours] ↗TechWorld with Nana3h · English
  • GitHub Actions documentation ↗GitHub DocsReference
  • Deployment guides ↗Vercel / Render / RailwayReference

💡 Choose the alternate capstone if you want a data + full-stack story. It is memorable in interviews and it doubles as market research for your own job hunt.

07
🗡️ DSA DOJO (DAILY) · Week 3–32 · 45 min/day

DSA & Problem Solving

⏱ 40h 0%

Kerala service companies and product companies both screen with aptitude + coding rounds. Consistency beats marathon weekends.

🐲 Boss to defeat: 150 curated problems solved + 2 timed mock coding rounds.

Watch / read (verified links)

  • Striver's A2Z DSA Sheet & Course ↗takeUforward450 items · free
  • Striver A2Z playlist ↗takeUforwardYouTube playlist
  • NeetCode Roadmap (optional) ↗NeetCodeFree · English

💡 Track problems in the Excel sheet. If a problem takes >35 min, read the editorial, then re-solve it 3 days later from scratch.

08
📊 BONUS BOSS ARC · Week 23–24 (only after capstone)

Power BI + Analytics

⏱ 30h 0%

This is your differentiator, not your core. Kerala service companies and data-adjacent roles love a dev who can also build a dashboard.

🐲 Boss to defeat: A 2-page Power BI dashboard published online + a 5-line business insight write-up on your portfolio.

Watch / read (verified links)

  • Power BI Project for Beginners (Sales Insights) ↗codebasics3h · English
  • Power BI Data Analyst (PL-300) certification path ↗Microsoft LearnOptional · free path
  • DAX overview ↗Microsoft LearnReference

💡 Do not start this before Season 6. Power BI is a multiplier on a full-stack profile — it cannot replace one.

09
🏁 JOB HUNT ENDGAME · Week 25–32

Portfolio, Resume & Offers

⏱ 100h 0%

Job hunting is a numbers game with a quality filter. 300 targeted applications + 30 referrals + 12 mock interviews is the formula.

🐲 Boss to defeat: A signed offer. Your first CTC is not your final form — your learning curve is.

Watch / read (verified links)

  • System Design Primer ↗GitHub · donnemartinReference
  • Frontend interview questions ↗GeeksforGeeksReference
  • Career + interview videos (Malayalam) ↗Brototype MalayalamChannel · Malayalam

💡 A referral is worth 20 cold applications. Your current internship colleagues are referral gold — ask them before you leave.

Daily operating system

Your 6-hour study day

Built around an internship. Split it, protect it, and never negotiate with the clock. Total: 24 study hours + 6 project hours = 30 hours/week.

Weekday template (Mon–Thu)

05:30 – 07:00
Deep work #1Video/reading at 1.25×, take notes by hand, no phone
07:00 – 08:00
Commute / audioReplay a concept in your head or listen to a podcast — no new material
19:00 – 20:30
Deep work #2Code along with the tutorial, then break it deliberately
20:30 – 21:30
Build from scratchClose the tutorial and rebuild the feature alone
21:30 – 22:15
DSA + review1–2 problems, then 10 minutes of flashcards
22:15 – 22:30
Log itTick the Excel tracker, commit to GitHub, one-line journal

The week

Mon–Thu
6 hours

Theory → code-along → build-alone → DSA → log

Friday
Project day

6+ hours of pure building. No new videos. Ship something.

Saturday
Recovery + 1h

Rest, family, gym. Optional: 1 hour of job-portal browsing.

Sunday
Recovery

Zero study guilt. Burnout is the real final boss.

⚔️ The 5 laws of this training arc

  • 70/30 rule: 70% building, 30% watching. Every video ends with the tab closed.
  • One boss per season: no new phase until the deliverable is deployed.
  • Daily commit: a green square is proof of life.
  • 45 min DSA daily from week 3 — not 5-hour Sunday marathons.
  • One rest day. Burnout is the real final boss.

Levi had no guarantee either. 25 applications a week — rejection is data, not a verdict on you.

📐 Application maths (be honest with yourself)

25 quality applications/week → ~300 over 12 weeks. A realistic 8–12% interview rate for freshers → 25–35 interviews → 3–5 final rounds → 1–2 offers.

The people who "applied to 20 jobs and got nothing" usually applied to 20 jobs. Volume + tailoring + referrals is the formula.

🤝 Referral message that works

Hi [Name], I'm a frontend intern moving into full-stack (MERN + TypeScript). I built [project + live link], a job board with JWT auth and 40+ REST endpoints. I saw [Company] is hiring for [role]. Would you be open to referring me — or pointing me to the right person? Happy to send my resume. Thanks either way!

Resume upgrades (before you apply anywhere)

Lead with projects, not duties

"Built a MERN job board with JWT auth serving 40+ REST endpoints" beats "Worked on frontend tasks".

Put the stack in the top third

Recruiters and ATS scan for React, Node, MongoDB, TypeScript, Git. Make them impossible to miss.

Add numbers

Users, endpoints, screens, response time, test coverage, number of components.

One page, one column

No photos, no skill bars, no 'references available'. ATS-friendly PDF.

Link everything

Live demo + GitHub + LinkedIn in the header. If it isn't clickable, it doesn't exist.

Turn your internship into backend evidence

Ask for one API task or bug-fix sprint, then write the measurable result.

Boss dialogue

Interview question bank

The questions Indian fresher panels actually ask. Answer each out loud — in English, then in Malayalam if that's your comfort language.

JavaScript — 10 questions
  1. What is a closure? Give a real use case.
  2. Difference between var, let and const, including hoisting and TDZ.
  3. Explain the event loop with a setTimeout + Promise example.
  4. Implement debounce and throttle.
  5. map vs forEach vs filter vs reduce — when do you use each?
  6. Explain `this` in arrow functions vs regular functions.
  7. Shallow vs deep copy — write a deep clone.
  8. What is event delegation and why is it useful?
  9. Explain promises vs async/await and error handling.
  10. Curry a function: sum(1)(2)(3).
React — 10 questions
  1. Why does React use keys? What breaks with index keys?
  2. Virtual DOM and reconciliation — explain simply.
  3. useEffect dependency array — what causes infinite loops?
  4. Controlled vs uncontrolled components.
  5. What does lifting state up mean? When is Context better?
  6. Write a custom hook for fetching data.
  7. useMemo vs useCallback vs React.memo — when does each help?
  8. How does React Router handle params and nested routes?
  9. How would you optimise a slow list of 1,000 items?
  10. Explain props drilling and two ways to avoid it.
Node / DB / API — 10 questions
  1. What is middleware in Express? Write an auth guard.
  2. JWT vs session cookies — trade-offs?
  3. How do you hash passwords and why bcrypt?
  4. How do you handle errors centrally in Express?
  5. SQL vs MongoDB — when would you pick each?
  6. What is an index? When does it slow writes down?
  7. Explain a JOIN with an example from your project.
  8. How do you prevent NoSQL injection / validate input?
  9. How would you design pagination for 1M records?
  10. Walk me through deploying your API.
HR / Behavioural — 10 questions
  1. Tell me about yourself (30 seconds, not 3 minutes).
  2. Why full stack, and why should we hire a fresher?
  3. Tell me about a bug that took you days. How did you find it?
  4. Describe a time you had to learn something fast.
  5. What did you do at your internship? (Quantify it.)
  6. Where do you see yourself in 2 years?
  7. Why our company, specifically?
  8. What are your salary expectations?
  9. How do you handle deadlines and pressure?
  10. Do you have any questions for us? (Always yes: team, code review, learning budget.)

Peer review · red-team pass

I had a second agent try to destroy this plan

Before shipping, I ran the plan through a hostile review whose only job was to find why it fails. These were the seven hits — and the fixes baked into the roadmap above.

You are trying to learn MERN + Python + Power BI + DSA in 6 months. That is how people burn out at month 3.

Sequence, don't parallelise. Python and Power BI are locked until the capstone ships. DSA is only 45 min/day.

Kerala's market is service-heavy: many Infopark JDs ask Java/Spring + Angular, not MERN.

Keep MERN as your primary (fastest given your JS base), add Python/Django basics for Kerala JDs, and learn Java in year 2 if you target enterprise.

Tutorial hell is the #1 killer. Watching 22 hours of JS while typing nothing feels productive.

70/30 rule: 70% of study time is building. Every video must end with the tab closed and code written from memory.

If you learn React before backend, you risk becoming a 'card designer' who freezes when asked about auth or databases.

Frontend first is fine, but your API must be live by week 12. Backend is where fresher offers are won.

Applying only in Kerala shrinks the pool to a few hundred roles and depresses your first salary.

Apply 70% Kerala (Infopark/Technopark/Cyberpark) + 30% Bengaluru/Chennai/Hyderabad/remote. Same effort, 5× the market.

DSA can eat your entire life and delay shipping.

150 curated problems, not 500. Patterns over volume. Stop DSA prep the week you have 3 interviews.

Your current internship is being wasted if you only do frontend tickets.

Ask your lead for one backend task, one bug-fix sprint, and one code review. Then put the measurable outcome on your resume.

Training-arc energy

You are not behind. You are at the start of the arc where the protagonist is still weak — and that's exactly where every good story begins.
